activities.anchor: most classroom hours go to reading and rule study
activities.caption: call the speed the ear must run at
activities.name: lciSpeedEstimate

config.prompt: Native speech arrives at roughly how many words per minute?
config.why: About 150-plus — no pause for the gap-filling a reader's eyes do, which is why listening is the highest-volume channel and the one learners most undertrain.
config.context: The method that closes the gap is comprehensible input: massive exposure to messages understood mostly.

activities.caption: pair each process with what drives it
activities.name: lciBrainMatch

config.prompt: The statistical machinery of comprehension — pair the process with its engine:

pairs.left: word segmentation out of the stream
patterns the grammar books later name
pairs.right: extracted without any rule being stated
noise — nothing to map onto, the statistics never fire

config.why: None of it needs the rules stated; it needs volume of understood messages — which is why noise is wasted hours.

activities.anchor: recalibrate monthly, because content that was i+1 in March is i+0 by September
activities.caption: place the sweet spot
activities.name: lciBandPlace

config.prompt: Known words per hundred, sampled from a transcript — where does the context-inference sweet spot sit?
config.why: About 90% known (ten unknowns per hundred): enough stretch to acquire, few enough gaps to bridge. Below 80% known, guessing collapses; near 100%, you are maintaining, not growing.
config.context: Staying in band beats staying loyal to a series that has outgrown you.

activities.anchor: you will get used to it
activities.caption: advise the deep-end diver
activities.name: lciDeepEndBranch

config.root: A friend announces a plan: all winter, nothing but native news, from day one.

choices.label: Go ahead — total immersion trains fastest
choices.feedback: Below the band, hours pass without a single message understood.

choices.label: Start in band and climb notch by notch
choices.feedback: Immersion works through comprehension, not proximity.

deep.text: Without enough known words there is nothing to infer from — the input is noise, however loud.

choices.label: Rewrite the plan
choices.feedback: The country works because messages become necessary, not because they are loud.

shallow.text: Near 100% known, you are maintaining, not growing — the band has an upper edge too.

choices.label: Rewrite the plan
choices.feedback: Climb when the count drops under five unknowns per hundred.

band.text: Stay in the band and let it carry you upward — recalibrated as it moves.

config.why: Immersion works through comprehension, not proximity — the deep end is a place, not a method.

activities.anchor: watch things about what you love
activities.caption: file each source on the ladder
activities.name: lciLadderBuckets

config.prompt: The ladder of sources — file each rung by level:

items.label: children's cartoons — deliberately simple, deliberately short
YouTube in your existing hobbies — lifting, cooking, code

config.why: Knowing the subject is a legitimate substitute for vocabulary; humour and cultural reference are the final milestones because they run on inference and shared knowledge.

config.prompt: One series, four passes — order the progression, first mode first:
items: none — the ear does all the work
rewatch the episodes you loved bare — confidence
config.why: Mitterer and McQueen (2009): same-language subtitles improve speech perception itself, while reversed-language subtitles actively interfere — choose the mode for the job you are training.

activities.anchor: The dictionary form and the acoustic form
activities.caption: find the line the word-list myth would love
activities.name: lciDecodeSpot

config.prompt: One line of this diagnosis is wrong — click it:
lines: Native speech is not words spoken faster; it is words physically changed.
Sounds delete ("camra"), merge ("wanna", "d'you"), assimilate ("ten bikes" → "tem bikes").
Vocabulary tests predict listening well — know the word on paper and you will hear it.
The fix is intensive listening with transcript comparison — meeting the reduced forms' fingerprints.
config.correction: Vocabulary tests fail to predict listening: you do not lack the word, you lack the reduced form's fingerprint.
config.why: After enough collisions the reductions become automatic — you stop hearing "gonna" as missing words and start hearing it as one word.

activities.anchor: they are all reachable from here
activities.caption: pair each stall with its fix
activities.name: lciStallMatch

config.prompt: Listening stalls — pair the symptom with the right lever:

pairs.left: slow audio fine, native speed impossible
pairs.right: decoding — intensive work on reduced forms, plus shadowing
form-mapping — read-then-listen cycles on known content
knowledge, not ear — change the content, not the method
out of band or out of interest — shorten sessions, raise interest

config.why: Diagnose before you push — applying the usual lever (just more volume) is what makes the stalls feel unfixable.
